review_candidates.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Project Risk Manager - EMEA based in Spain. Lead risk management across a complex EMEA project portfolio supporting the delivery of large-scale AI infrastructure. You will establish consistent risk governance while providing hands-on expertise across project, portfolio, commercial, cost, and schedule risk. Working alongside project directors, engineers, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations teams, you will help make uncertainty visible and actionable. You will lead qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, including Monte Carlo simulations, schedule risk analysis, scenario modelling, and contingency assessment. The role combines independent assurance with close business partnership, giving you influence over major project and investment decisions. You will identify systemic and correlated risks across the regional portfolio and translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for senior leadership. This is a high-impact opportunity for an experienced risk professional who thrives in fast-paced, technically complex, and rapidly scaling infrastructure environments. Accountabilities Lead the regional project risk management programme across the EMEA portfolio, establishing consistent governance, standards, processes, methodologies, and escalation requirements. Embed risk management throughout the project lifecycle and across Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Controls, Commercial, Commissioning, and Operations Readiness. Provide independent risk oversight and constructive challenge to project and functional leadership, ensuring significant risks and opportunities receive appropriate attention. Promote a proactive risk culture based on early identification, clear ownership, accountability, timely escalation, and risk-informed decision-making. Act as the regional subject matter expert and trusted adviser on project and portfolio risk for project, regional, and executive leadership. Lead the identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, escalation, and closure of project risks and opportunities. Build, maintain, and oversee project risk registers, ensuring material risks have clear owners, mitigation strategies, action plans, residual assessments, and escalation paths. Assess delivery risks across design, permitting, grid connection, procurement, long-lead equipment, construction, commercial and contractual performance, commissioning, energisation, and capacity delivery. Consolidate project-level risks at regional level to identify emerging, systemic, correlated, and concentration risks requiring portfolio-wide action. Promote the identification and realization of opportunities relating to cost, schedule, standardisation, procurement, constructability, and overall project execution. Lead qualitative and quantitative cost and schedule risk analysis, including Monte Carlo simulation, Schedule Risk Analysis (SRA), scenario analysis, and other probabilistic techniques. Assess cost exposure, schedule uncertainty, critical-path risks, key milestones, and confidence in achieving committed delivery and ready-for-service dates. Develop risk-based recommendations for project contingency and management reserves and support governance over their utilization and release. Analyse regional risk drivers, correlations, scenarios, and sensitivities to identify potential portfolio impacts and mitigation priorities. Provide risk analysis and recommendations for investment decisions, stage gates, baseline approvals, major contract awards, and other significant project decisions. Produce concise project and regional reporting covering top risks and opportunities, emerging exposures, trends, mitigation effectiveness, contingency status, and matters requiring escalation. Develop risk dashboards and analytics that provide visibility into exposure, trends, concentrations, and confidence across cost, schedule, commissioning, and capacity commitments. Monitor mitigation progress, overdue actions, changes in exposure, realised risks, and significant issues requiring project, regional, or executive attention. Conduct periodic project risk reviews and health checks to assess the quality and effectiveness of risk identification, analysis, mitigation, reporting, and governance. Independently test project assumptions, forecasts, contingency requirements, mitigation strategies, and confidence levels to ensure material exposures are understood and communicated appropriately. Identify recurring risks, systemic weaknesses, successful mitigation strategies, and lessons learned across projects and incorporate them into future delivery approaches. Drive continuous improvement across risk processes, methodologies, tools, analytics, reporting, and organisational risk capability. Requirements Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, Finance, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant industry experience. Significant professional experience in risk management, project controls, or project delivery within complex EPC, construction, infrastructure, energy, mission-critical, or major capital programmes. Demonstrated experience leading project and portfolio risk management, including identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, escalation, and assurance. Strong understanding of cost, schedule, contingency, and project controls principles and how they integrate with project risk management. Advanced experience applying quantitative risk analysis and probabilistic techniques to assess project cost and schedule uncertainty. Strong hands-on experience with Monte Carlo simulation, cost and schedule risk analysis, scenario analysis, and risk-based contingency development. Strong understanding of EPC contracting, procurement, supply chain, change management, claims, and commercial risk. Proven ability to influence and constructively challenge senior project and functional leaders in complex, fast-moving environments. Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex risk information into clear business insights and recommended actions. Ability to identify systemic and correlated risks across multiple projects and provide regional-level insight to support management decisions. Experience delivering hyperscale, AI, mission-critical, or large-scale data centre programmes is advantageous. Familiarity with power, cooling, grid connections, long-lead equipment, commissioning, and capacity delivery is a plus. Experience with enterprise or project risk management platforms and their integration with scheduling, cost management, and reporting systems is beneficial. Relevant professional certification such as PMI-RMP, PMP, APM PMQ or ChPP, AACE International, IRM, or an equivalent risk or project management credential is advantageous. Working knowledge of recognised risk management frameworks, including ISO 31000 and PMBOK, with familiarity with standards such as ISO 9001, ISO 45001, and ISO 14001. Experience presenting portfolio risk, contingency, schedule confidence, and emerging exposures to executive leadership or governance committees. Experience with @Risk, Riskonnect, Safran, or comparable industry-standard risk management tools is a plus. Strong analytical thinking, sound judgement, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills. Benefits Competitive salary based on the scope and value of the role rather than previous compensation. Equity opportunity, allowing eligible employees to participate in the organisation's long-term growth. Discretionary bonus opportunity. Retirement or pension contributions. review_candidates.title: National Strategic Communications Consultant
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women in Georgia supports state and non-state partners towards the achievement of substantive gender equality in Georgia. In line with national and international commitments, UN Women works on the levels of policy and legislation, institutions and grassroots, in order to achieve transformative results for increased gender equality and greater protection of the rights of women and girls. UN Women puts special emphasis on the work towards gender mainstreaming in good governance reforms and enhancing women’s political participation, ending violence against women, promoting and supporting women’s economic empowerment, and Women, Peace and Security agenda. Globally, progress towards gender equality and women’s rights is taking place in an increasingly challenging environment, characterized by shrinking civic space, growing political and social polarization, increasing pressures on civil society, and intensifying backlash against gender equality. Women’s civil society organizations (CSOs), Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs), feminist activists and other actors working to advance women’s rights are particularly affected by these developments, facing growing constraints on their ability to participate, organize, advocate and influence public discourse. A significant dimension of the growing backlash against gender equality is the increasing prominence of anti-gender narratives in public and political discourse. Such narratives challenge the legitimacy and relevance of gender equality and women’s rights, reinforce harmful gender stereotypes, and contribute to misinformation and polarization. They frequently portray gender equality as being in conflict with traditional, cultural, religious and family values; question the existence or extent of gender inequality and violence against women; and seek to discredit women’s rights organizations, activists and other actors advancing gender equality. In this context, strengthening strategic communication and developing credible, accessible and context-sensitive positive narratives on gender equality, women’s rights and women’s leadership is increasingly important. Georgia is not immune to these trends. Anti-gender narratives have become increasingly prominent in public and political discourse, compounded by shrinking civic space, growing pressure on gender equality advocates, and restrictions affecting women’s rights organizations that have long served as the backbone of the country’s gender equality agenda. As these narratives become more normalized and persuasive, they risk shaping public attitudes and influencing the perceptions of communities, institutions and decision-makers. Their growing resonance threatens to erode public support for gender equality and women’s rights, undermine trust in women’s organizations and activists, and reverse hard-won progress towards substantive gender equality. Within the framework of its Women’s Leadership and Decision-making (WLD) portfolio, UN Women, with the generous support of the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), is implementing the “Women’s Increased Leadership for Democracy in Georgia” project. Within this framework, UN Women seeks to engage a National Strategic Communications Consultant to provide technical support for developing strategic communication messages to counter anti-gender narratives and advance positive narratives on gender equality, women’s rights and women’s leadership, thereby strengthening responses to anti-gender narratives in Georgia. The consultancy will build substantially on the findings and recommendations of UN Women’s recent report on anti-gender narratives in Georgia, which will serve as a key analytical foundation for the assignment. The consultant will work closely with UN Women and facilitate a participatory process to identify priority communication challenges and audiences and develop context-sensitive narratives and messages. The proposed messages will be tested with different audience groups to assess their clarity, relevance, credibility and resonance, and will subsequently be refined based on the results of the testing and consultations with relevant stakeholders. The National Consultant will be reporting to the WLD Project Analyst and WLD Programme Specialist and will be supported by the WLD Project Assistant, who will be the point of contact on the contract and payment issues. Description Of Responsibilities/ Scope Of Work Conduct a desk review of relevant reports, research, communication materials and other background documents to assess the current communication landscape and the dynamics of anti-gender narratives and public perceptions related to gender equality in Georgia. Hold consultations with relevant professionals, including representatives of civil society organizations, communication experts and other key stakeholders, to better understand the evolving narrative environment, audience dynamics and communication opportunities. Develop evidence-based strategic narratives and key messages on gender equality, women’s rights and women’s leadership, and test the proposed messages with selected target audiences to assess their relevance, clarity, credibility and resonance. Refine and finalize the tested narratives and messages based on the findings from audience testing and stakeholder consultations. By 26 October 2026 (5 days) Message testing completed and narrative and messaging framework finalized, including testing with selected audience groups, analysis of findings and refinement of narratives and key messages. By 09 November 2026 (3 days) A finalized package of strategic narratives and key messages, incorporating findings from message testing and feedback from UN Women and the Task Force on Women’s Leadership, together with practical guidance for their use in communication and advocacy efforts. By 23 November 2026 (3 days) Consultant’s Workplace and Official Travel As part of this assignment, travel in Georgia will not be necessary. Statements: In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women.
